test_title: PYST 05: SSC Stenographer - English Language & Comprehension (Held On: 11 Dec 2024 - Shift 2)
subject: english
question:
Select the option that expresses the following sentence in indirect speech.

“I have not completed the assignment yet,” the student admitted.

options.text: The student admitted that he/she hadn’t completed the assignment yet.
The student admitted that he/she hasn’t completed the assignment yet
The student admitted that he/she hasn't been able to complete the assignment yet.
The student admitted that he/she hadn’t been able to complete the assignment yet.

solution:
The correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• When converting direct speech into indirect speech:
 
• The reporting verb "admitted" suggests that the tense needs to be changed to the past form.
 
• The present perfect tense "have not completed" in direct speech changes to "had not completed" in indirect speech.
 
• "Yet" remains unchanged in indirect speech.
 
• Pronouns may change based on context ("I" changes to "he/she").

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"The student admitted that he/she hadn’t completed the assignment yet."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 2:** "The student admitted that he/she hasn’t completed the assignment yet." – Incorrect because the present perfect tense "hasn’t completed" should be changed to the past perfect "hadn’t completed" in indirect speech.
 
• **Option 3:** "The student admitted that he/she hasn't been able to complete the assignment yet." – Incorrect because "hasn't been able to complete" remains in the present perfect, which should shift to past perfect.
 
• **Option 4:** "The student admitted that he/she hadn’t been able to complete the assignment yet." – Incorrect because "hadn’t been able to complete" changes the meaning slightly by emphasizing inability rather than incompletion.
